themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 7 THIS WEEK, up 409% from the 8-week baseline of 1.4 weekly complaints (z-score: 5.67), suggesting a coordinated or sudden wave of unauthorized signage across Forest Hills/Rego Park.
evidence: 7 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (409% spike)
Z-score of 5.67 indicates statistically significant anomaly
No prior recent spike in this category suggests sudden emergence
reporting_angles: Are there specific corridors or neighborhoods within Forest Hills/Rego Park where posting is concentrated? (identify clusters via 311 geo-tagging)
Interview Parks Dept. or CB enforcement staff: is this linked to a campaign, event promotion, or illegal contractor activity?

themes_detail.label: Panhandling Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Panhandling complaints nearly 9x the baseline this week, with 7 complaints reported LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (833% increase, z-score: 9.45), the highest-severity spike in the district's recent data.
evidence: 7 panhandling complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (833% spike)
Highest z-score (9.45) among all spikes, indicating extreme statistical anomaly
Sustained emergence: shift from near-zero complaints to significant volume
reporting_angles: Interview residents and local merchants: have they observed an increase in panhandling intensity, locations, or organized activity?
Contact NYPD and social services: is there a homelessness surge, displacement from adjacent areas, or seasonal pattern?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle Noise Peak
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints hit 18 THREE WEEKS AGO, up 148% from the 7.2 weekly average (z-score: 4.08), indicating possible illegal street racing, loud exhaust modifications, or construction noise concentrated in one or two weeks.
evidence: 18 vehicle noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 7.2 weekly average (148% spike)
Z-score of 4.08 indicates significant statistical anomaly
Noise - Residential (973 complaints) is second-largest complaint category overall, suggesting broader noise stress in district
reporting_angles: Identify specific streets or times of day from 311 data: are complaints clustered (e.g., late night, specific avenue)?
Interview residents on affected blocks: are they experiencing organized street racing, construction noise, or modified vehicle traffic?

themes_detail.label: Maintenance & Facility Decline
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints reached 19 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 138% from the 8-week average of 8.0 (z-score: 3.83), suggesting deteriorating park, street furniture, or public facility conditions across the district.
evidence: 19 maintenance/facility complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 8.0 weekly average (138% increase)
Street Condition (970 complaints) is third-highest category over 90 days, reinforcing infrastructure stress
reporting_angles: Map 311 complaints by facility type: are issues concentrated in parks, subway stations, traffic signals, or street furniture?
Contact Parks Dept. and DOE: are budget cuts or staffing shortages delaying maintenance in Forest Hills/Rego Park?

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Spike
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 4 TWO WEEKS AGO, up 433% from the 0.8 weekly baseline (z-score: 3.92), suggesting either increased unlicensed vendor activity or community friction around street vending.
evidence: 4 vendor enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average (433% spike)
Z-score of 3.92 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Baseline so low suggests this is an emerging or re-emerging issue, not chronic
reporting_angles: What types of vendors are driving complaints? (food carts, merchandise, etc.) Check 311 complaint text.
Interview business owners and residents: are they concerned about safety, sanitation, or unfair competition from unlicensed vendors?
